target.projectDescription: Distributed computing framework (Python API on top of a C++ core). The Python attack surface in this snapshot: an aiohttp-based dashboard (head server on the driver node + agent server on every node, under the repo-root dashboard/ directory), gRPC services (reporter agent, ray client server under python/ray/util/client/server/), the Ray Jobs submission API (dashboard job module executes submitted entrypoints as shell commands), Ray Serve (aiohttp/Starlette ingress and a serve dashboard module), the autoscaler (cluster config YAML drives ssh/docker command execution on cluster nodes), runtime_env setup (conda/pip/venv subprocess execution), and a large click-based CLI (ray/scripts/scripts.py).

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face (1) the dashboard head HTTP API (default port 8265, no authentication in this snapshot): job submission fields (entrypoint shell command, runtime_env conda/pip/env_vars, submission_id), serve deployment configs, node/actor/state/log query parameters, and the py-spy profiling parameters (pid, duration, format) that reach a shell command; (2) the dashboard agent HTTP API on every node (job_agent, serve_agent, log_agent routes); (3) gRPC services: the reporter service (CpuProfiling/GetTraceback request fields) and the ray client server (client-supplied protobuf payloads, deserialized server-side); (4) Ray Serve per-deployment HTTP ingress (Starlette request bodies/params passed to user code); (5) CLI arguments (click options/arguments incl. cluster config files) and environment variables (RAY_* and third-party vars such as EDITOR, 446 os.environ/os.getenv read sites); (6) the user-supplied cluster config YAML consumed by the autoscaler, whose ssh/docker/command fields are executed on cluster nodes. Command execution sinks: subprocess.Popen (job entrypoint with shell=True), asyncio.create_subprocess_shell (py-spy profiling commands built from request pid/duration/format), the autoscaler process_runner check_call/check_output ssh/docker pipeline, runtime_env conda/pip subprocess execution, os.execvp worker replacement, and a set of smaller subprocess sites.

sinkFamilies.evidence: no os.system / os.popen / os.spawn* call exists in non-test project source; the only os.exec* site is runtime_env/context.py:95 os.execvp (covered above). The query keeps the standard CWE-78 API set (subprocess.*, os.system/popen/exec*/spawn*) for exhaustiveness; expected real rows: subprocess family + os.execvp + asyncio.create_subprocess_*

sanitizerObservations: autoscaler uses shlex.quote on selected command fragments: command_runner.py:9 'from shlex import quote', docker.py:7, commands.py:77 - e.g. _with_environment_variables (command_runner.py:86) quotes environment-variable values into the ssh command; quoting is per-fragment, and SSHCommandRunner.run still appends raw caller cmd strings (:304-309 'cmd += "; sudo shutdown -h now"')

dashboard job pipeline validates request shape only: pydantic/dataclass validation in utils.py parse_and_validate_request and pydantic_models.py:67 'entrypoint: str = Field(...)' - entrypoint is typed as a free string with no shell metacharacter neutralization; the job entrypoint is BY DESIGN an arbitrary shell command (job submission is an authenticated-admin feature in later Ray versions; this snapshot has no dashboard authentication)

reporter_head.py converts some query values with int() (e.g. :348 'duration = int(req.query.get("duration", 5))', :416 'pid = int(req.query["pid"])') before sending them over gRPC - integer coercion is a partial sanitizer for those specific fields; 'format' (:351) is passed through as a string into the py-spy command f-string
no shlex.quote/pipes.quote wrapping exists in the job entrypoint path (job_manager.py:229) or the py-spy profiling path (profile_manager.py:69-107)
autoscaler cluster configs are schema-checked/filled (fillout_defaults/validate) before use - structure validation, not command neutralization
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Ray Jobs and Ray Serve are user-facing execution features: a submitted job entrypoint is intended to run an arbitrary command on the cluster, and serve deployments run user code by design. These sites are recorded as sink candidates for CWE-78 flow analysis (the security question is which network boundary can reach them), not automatically as vulnerabilities. Likewise the static probe commands (ps/nvidia-smi/sysctl-style, 'ray stack' script, sudo -n true) and internal-pid watchdog commands are platform introspection with static or internal operands.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile, then codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) and codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF (per instruction, CodeQL is not run in this step - the queries are generated only)
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, parameter position for 'param' rows, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules (json, yaml, os, subprocess, asyncio)
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver/variable name); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise. Dynamic receiver boundaries in this codebase resolve only at AST level: the autoscaler process_runner.check_output/check_call attribute calls (process_runner is an injected module variable), the req.query/req.match_info request reads, grpc message-field reads (request.pid), and pydantic Schema.parse_obj calls

exclusions: test locations: any path under a tests/ directory or conftest.py (dashboard/modules/*/tests, python/ray/tests, rllib tests, etc.) are excluded in both queries

documentation and benchmark trees are not present as python source in the database in significant volume; serve/benchmarks and experimental raysort/benchmarks remain included because they are runnable module code, not test fixtures
logging-only helpers and pure response writers are not extracted as candidates

uncoveredCases: f-string command construction is not captured by the cmd_format sink family: this python-all version exposes no FormattedString AST class, and f-strings (profile_manager.py:69/99 py-spy commands, DockerCommandRunner.run_rsync_up:510-516 mkdir/chown commands, job_manager.py:258 kill watchdog) are therefore only represented by their sink call rows, not as separate cmd_format rows

dynamic process_runner dispatch: autoscaler command execution bottoms out in attribute calls on a module-valued variable (command_runner.py:279, subprocess_output_util.py:243); the callee module (subprocess vs a test fake) is not resolvable, captured as flow_kind 'indirect_exec' with moduleHint '<dynamic-process-runner>'

dynamic cmd_runner dispatch in updater.py:230/284/422/481/523 'self.cmd_runner.run(cmd, ...)' resolves to SSHCommandRunner/DockerCommandRunner only via runtime config; '.run' is too generic for an AST match, so the autoscaler chain is covered by the SSHCommandRunner._run_helper exec sites and internal_exec_wrapper rows instead of the .run call sites

gRPC servicer methods are detected by their (self, request*, context) signature shape rather than by resolved base classes (the generated *_pb2_grpc modules are not part of the extracted source tree), so a non-servicer method with an identical signature would also match

ray client server deserialization (server_pickler.py / client_pickler.py cloudpickle round-trips of client-supplied payloads) is an unsafe-deserialization boundary (CWE-502 territory); for CWE-78 it is recorded only via the servicer 'param' and 'message' rows
Ray core task arguments (worker.py receives deserialized task args from the C++ raylet) cross the python/C++ boundary below AST visibility; not represented as candidate rows

Bare-name (from-import) execution sinks are only matched for distinctive names (system, popen, getoutput, getstatusoutput); bare run/call/Popen/check_call are too collision-prone. In this repository every subprocess site is attribute-qualified except ConsolePopen (matched by name) and the from-imported helpers are only list2cmdline (not an exec API)

CLI cluster_config_file content reaches the executors only through yaml.safe_load rows plus the autoscaler function bodies; the config-field-to-command-field mapping (ssh_user, docker container_name, init commands) is data-driven through dicts and is not representable as AST candidate rows
